main.claim: Type an idea, pick a style, and get a LinkedIn post of 120 to 220 words in about 1 to 3 seconds. The post opens with a hook, uses short lines, and ends with a line that invites a reply. Free: 3 runs a day, no account, one-click copy.

sections.heading: How to write a LinkedIn post
sections.body:
Start with the idea, not the post. One or two sentences about what happened, what you learned, or what you think is enough. The tool turns that into a full draft in the style you pick.

1. Open the [LinkedIn post generator](https://linkedin-post.lazur.app/).
2. Type your idea in your own words. Add a number or a name if you have one.
3. Pick a style: Story, Lesson learned, Hot take, How-to list or Announcement.
4. Run the generator and wait a few seconds. Most answers come back in about 1 to 3 seconds.
5. Copy the draft with one click, paste it into LinkedIn, and edit it.

You can also add a file up to 15 MB as the source for your post.

sections.heading: Pick the style that fits your idea
sections.body:
The style sets the shape of the post. Pick the one that matches what you want a reader to take away.

- **Story:** a moment from your work, told with a before and an after.
- **Lesson learned:** something you got wrong or found out, and what you would do next time.
- **Hot take:** one view you hold, stated plainly, with the reason behind it.
- **How-to list:** a short set of steps or tips a reader can use today.
- **Announcement:** a launch, a new role, a result or an event, with the next step.

If the first draft has the wrong shape, run it again with a different style. Keep the same idea so you can compare the two drafts side by side.

sections.heading: What every draft includes
sections.body:
Each draft is 120 to 220 words, short enough to read on a phone. The first line is written to make someone stop scrolling, so it states the point instead of warming up. Lines are short, and each post covers one idea.

The post ends with a line that invites a reply, such as a question or a request for other views. Hashtags are kept to 3 at the end, so you get a few tags, not a wall of them.

**Read the first line first.** If it does not sound like you, change it before anything else. The rest of the post usually follows the same voice.

sections.heading: Check and edit before you post
sections.body:
A draft is a starting point. The tool writes from your idea, so it can get details wrong or sound generic. Before you post:

1. Check every fact, number and name against what actually happened.
2. Replace any sentence that anyone could have written. Add one detail only you know.
3. Remove any claim about a result you cannot show.
4. Read it out loud. If a line is hard to say, cut it.

A shorter post built on your real experience works better than a longer draft you did not check.

sections.heading: Free runs and what they cost you
sections.body:
The generator is free and needs no account or sign-up to start. You get 3 runs a day. If you leave an email, you get 3 more runs.

Each run gives you a new draft, so use a run when you have a real idea to test, not to try every word. Copy your best draft somewhere safe before you start the next run.

sections.heading: Post more often without starting from zero
sections.body:
If you write posts every week, keep a short list of ideas in a notes app. Each idea is one or two sentences, and each one can become a post in a different style. Run the same idea as a Story and as a Lesson learned, then keep the version that sounds most like you.

If you dictate or write posts every day, Lazur does this in any app on your Mac. Hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).
